## Upgrading to 5.0

Most of what changes in 5.0 makes a default safer. Check the points below that
apply to you; everything else upgrades without changes.

### Server

- **CORS patterns that match more than they look like are refused at startup.**
  `https://example.com*` also allowed `https://example.com.attacker.test`,
  `*example.com` allowed `https://notexample.com`, and a scheme-less
  `*.example.com` allowed `http://` as well as `https://`. The error names the
  replacement for each pattern: `https://*.example.com` for subdomains,
  `https://example.com:*` for any port, or an anchored regex such as
  `/^https:\/\/dev-.*$/`. An unanchored regex is refused too; wrap it in `^…$`.
- **`allowed_origins: ["*"]` (the default) now answers with a literal `*`**
  instead of echoing the request's `Origin`, so responses can be cached once
  for every origin.
- **Symlinks that point outside a served folder are refused.** Pass
  `--follow-symlinks` or set `server.follow_symlinks: true` to serve them.
- **Responses carry `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`.** Set it in
  `extra_response_headers` to override it.

### Converting

- **Writing to a directory replaces its contents** instead of merging into them,
  so a smaller re-run leaves no stale tiles behind. A destination directory that
  is not empty is refused unless you pass `--force`.
- **Outputs appear only when they are complete.** A file is written beside its
  destination and moved into place at the end; if the conversion fails, the
  previous file is left as it was. An output that finished but is missing tiles
  is kept as `name.incomplete.ext` instead of under the name you asked for.

### TileJSON

- **Merged sources are combined as peers.** When a pipeline merges several
  sources, the first source to set a value now keeps it: an overlay merged into
  a base tileset no longer replaces the base's `name`, `type`, `version` or
  `center` (#276). `attribution` and `description` are still combined, and
  `tiles`, `data` and `grids` are dropped from the merged result, since they
  describe where one source's tiles live.

### Node.js

- **Node.js 22 or newer is required.** Node 16, 18 and 20 are end-of-life.

### Rust library

- **Rust 1.95 or newer is required.**
- **The library no longer installs a panic hook or signal handlers.** An
  application that wants the terminal progress indicator cleared on a crash or
  Ctrl-C calls `versatiles_container::install_terminal_reset_hooks()` itself, as
  the `versatiles` CLI does.
